title: Model paragraphs in three perspectives
subject: English
source: Written for english/y7 lesson 50 (Model paragraphs in three perspectives (teacher-written, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 50: Grammar: pronouns, perspective and inclusive language. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Third person
paras: They had ten minutes to leave. They took only what they could carry: a coat each, a bag of bread and a photograph of their grandfather. The boy looked back once at the door. Then they walked into the dark.

passage.title: First person plural
paras: We had ten minutes to leave. We took only what we could carry: a coat each, a bag of bread and the photograph of Grandad that always hung by the stairs. I looked back once at our green door, the one I had kicked a hundred times with my football. Then we walked into the dark.

passage.title: Second person
paras: You have ten minutes to leave. You take only what you can carry. You look back once at your door, and you wonder who will close it now. Then you walk into the dark.

blocks.h: Rewrite this in the first person

passage.title: For you to rewrite
paras: She packed her schoolbooks first. Her mother told her there was no room, so she chose one: the book with her name inside the cover. At the border, a soldier asked her name. She showed him the book.

head: Not this
This
rows: Families arrive and become our neighbours.

model.title: Rewrite in the first person plural: 'They had ten minutes to leave. They took only what they could carry.'

parts.text: Change the verbs if needed: we had, we took
Add one detail only an insider would know

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: We had ten minutes to leave. We took only what we could carry, and my brother would not let go of my hand.

keywords.def: a word that stands in for a noun: I, you, she, we, they
told by the speaker: I, we
words that bring everyone in and leave no one out

questions.q: Change to second person: 'A refugee leaves home with almost nothing.'
questions.a: You leave home with almost nothing.

questions.q: Replace the excluding phrase with inclusive language: 'Those foreigners in our school.'
questions.a: For example: 'The new pupils in our school.'

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, rewrite the third-person paragraph on the sheet in the first person, adding two details only the speaker would know. Starter: 'I remember...'
questions.a: A first-person rewrite, consistent pronouns, two personal details.

questions.q: Extend: write one sentence explaining which version has more impact and why
questions.a: For example: first person, because we share the boy's fear from inside.

questions.q: Stretch: write a two-sentence appeal for a school charity collection using 'we' and 'you' deliberately
questions.a: For example: 'We have more than we need. You can turn one spare coat into one warm winter for a child.'

questions.q: A charity leaflet says 'You can give a family a safe night'. Why 'you'?
options: to sound like a story about someone else
to speak directly to the reader and make them feel responsible
because the writer forgot the name
questions.a: B) to speak directly to the reader and make them feel responsible. Second person addresses the reader, so the appeal feels personal.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: how does one pronoun change who a text speaks to?
questions.a: For example: 'we' includes the reader; 'they' keeps them outside.
